commitResults.messageTitle: Add date-time parsing and resilient storage loading
commitResults.messageBody:
Store deadline and event timestamps as LocalDateTime values, accept ISO-style date and time input, and render them in a friendly format.

Validate impossible dates and reversed event ranges. Preserve startup when saved data is malformed by skipping corrupted records while loading valid tasks.

Expand UI persistence tests to cover valid and invalid date handling, legacy records, corrupted data, and delimiter-safe storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-7: add date-time parsing and resilient storage
commitResults.messageBody: Integrate typed deadline and event timestamps, date validation, corruption-tolerant data loading, and expanded UI coverage into master.

Accept d/M/yyyy dates with optional HHmm times alongside the existing ISO formats, allowing commands such as 2/12/2019 1800 while preserving the unambiguous storage format.

Update UI coverage for slash-formatted dates, impossible dates, and clearer format guidance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8: support flexible date input
commitResults.messageBody: Integrate day/month/year date parsing alongside ISO formats so Pathfinder understands inputs such as 2/12/2019 1800 while retaining strict validation and compatible storage.

Move standard-input reading, separators, greetings, responses, task-added feedback, and the farewell out of Pathfinder into a cohesive Ui class.

This reduces Pathfinder's presentation responsibilities while deliberately preserving its current command orchestration, keeping the first OOP extraction small and behaviour-compatible. All nine Java 25 UI cases pass unchanged.

Move command-word normalization, argument validation, task-number parsing, and todo, deadline, and event construction out of Pathfinder into a stateless Parser class.

Keep command execution and persistence in Pathfinder for this increment, creating a stable parsing boundary for the upcoming Command hierarchy without changing console behaviour. All nine Java 25 UI cases pass unchanged.

Move Pathfinder classes beneath the pathfinder base package, grouping parsing, storage, tasks, UI, utilities, and exceptions by responsibility while retaining src/main/java as the source root.

Update imports, IntelliJ setup documentation, and the UI test configuration. Teach the test runner to discover packaged sources recursively and launch the fully qualified main class. All nine Java 25 UI cases pass unchanged.

Point the Gradle application plugin at pathfinder.Pathfinder and rename the Shadow JAR from duke.jar to pathfinder.jar so the packaged application uses the project's actual entry point and identity.

Verified with JDK 25 using both gradlew build and an interactive gradlew run session.

Add focused tests for command parsing, date-time conversion, and task persistence, including invalid inputs, boundary cases, legacy data, and corrupted records. Document the project policy to maintain JUnit coverage for the highest-value methods after code changes.

Describe every public class, constructor, and method, including parameters, return values, and failure conditions. Document non-trivial private parsing, persistence, and command-handling helpers so generated API documentation explains the design and behavioral contracts.

Several classes use inconsistent naming, mutable fields, and formatting
that does not follow the project coding standard.

Rename ToDoTask to TodoTask, clarify task field and collection names,
make unchanging fields final, and align switch cases and imports with
SE-EDU conventions. Add missing API comments so the code is easier to
read and maintain without changing behavior.

Update affected parser and storage tests to use the corrected class
name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add SE-EDU Java coding standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Java changes need a consistent source of project-specific style rules.

Add a project skill that summarizes the SE-EDU standard and links to
the authoritative guide. Require agents to invoke it for production
and test Java changes so future edits remain consistent.

Commit and branch conventions need a shared project-specific source.

Add a project skill that defines compliant subjects, explanatory
bodies, and branch names. Require agents to invoke it before proposing
or creating commits so repository history remains clear.
Allow users to find tasks using case-insensitive description keywords. Handle missing keywords and no-match results with Pathfinder-style feedback, and cover the behavior with JUnit and UI tests.
Bring the documented Pathfinder APIs into master so public classes and non-trivial methods are easier to understand and maintain.

Apply SE-EDU Java conventions across production and test code.

Add project-specific Java and Git skills.

Require future code and commits to follow those standards.

Master lacks the Level 9 task-search feature.

Add case-insensitive description search and its automated tests.

Keep the feature history visible with a non-fast-forward merge.

Automated style checks are not part of the Gradle build, so coding
standard regressions can go unnoticed.

Add the SE-EDU Checkstyle configuration and enable Checkstyle 11.0.0.
Reformat existing assertion calls so production and test sources pass
the configured checks.

Multi-line responses are assembled with embedded newline characters,
which makes their structure harder to read and reuse.

Allow the UI to accept a variable number of response lines. Pass each
line separately while preserving the chatbot's existing console output.

Pathfinder only exposes commands through console output.

Expose command responses for the GUI while retaining the console
entry point. Add the FXML interface, required runtime dependencies,
and focused response tests so both interfaces use the same task logic.
Integrate Checkstyle validation after completing the branch work.
Integrate the completed varargs UI change through its own branch.
Integrate the completed JavaFX interface after finishing Level 10.

Task construction, command parsing, and state transitions rely on
conditions established by earlier validation. Violations can otherwise
fail later with less useful errors.

Add assertions for valid descriptions, parser dispatch, event
ordering, task indexes, and mark/unmark state changes. Verify these
assumptions with focused unit tests while retaining user-facing
validation.

Pathfinder stores tasks in ArrayList, leaving the custom List class
unreferenced. Its name also conflicts with java.util.List, while its
fixed capacity and console output obscure the active design.

Remove the dead class to reduce misleading code and keep the task
package focused on domain objects. This preserves behavior because no
source or test uses the class.

Command parsing uses normalized strings and never references the Inputs
enum. Keeping a second, inactive command representation makes the
parser package harder to understand and suggests a design dependency
that does not exist.

Remove the unused enum so the package exposes only the command model
used by the application. This reduces dead code without changing
runtime behavior.

Task is the only implementation of Describable, and no code accepts
or stores the interface type. The abstraction therefore adds a
navigation step without providing substitution or reuse.

Remove the interface and let Task expose getDescription() directly.
Keep the method signature unchanged so parser, storage, and search
behavior remain unaffected.

Pathfinder formats add-task responses before passing them to Ui, so
Ui.showTaskAdded is never called. The duplicate formatter also creates
an unnecessary dependency from the console UI to Task.

Remove the dead method and its import to keep Ui focused on generic
input/output operations. This preserves console behavior because all
add-task messages continue through showMessage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename task status methods for clarity
commitResults.messageBody:
Task.doTask and Task.undoTask sound as though they execute or reverse
a task, but they only update its completion flag. This makes
state-changing call sites harder to understand.

Rename the methods to markAsDone and markAsIncomplete, and update all
production and test callers. Preserve the existing state transitions
and persistence behavior while making intent explicit.

DateTimeParser.parseInput repeats the same try/catch structure for
each supported input format. The repetition hides format precedence
and requires copying control flow whenever a format changes.

Group related formatters and iterate through them in the existing order.
Keep date-time parsing ahead of date-only parsing and preserve strict
validation, midnight conversion, and the user-facing error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams to filter and format matches
commitResults.messageBody:
Finding tasks uses a mutable counter and StringBuilder while manually
filtering descriptions and trimming a trailing newline. This obscures
the two operations: selecting matches and formatting their positions.

Use a task stream to filter descriptions case-insensitively and an
IntStream to format matches with stable numbering. Add a focused test
to protect encounter order, case handling, and renumbering.
Add assertions for internal invariants

Bring the assertion work from master into the code-quality branch so
the branch builds on the latest shared history.

Resolve the task-status method conflict by retaining the clearer
markAsDone and markAsIncomplete names while preserving assertions that
verify status transitions and rollback behavior.

Bring assertion checks from master into the streams branch so the
stream refactoring remains based on the latest shared history.

Keep the stream-based filtering and formatting unchanged while adding
assertions and their focused tests for internal invariants.

commitResults.messageBody:
Bring the CodeQuality refactorings from master into the Streams branch
so it is based on the latest shared history.

Preserve the stream-based task search and the existing assertions while
adopting clearer task status names, removing unused abstractions, and
reducing duplicate date parsing logic.

Tasks cannot express relative importance, so users cannot record which
items need attention first.

Add a standalone priority command with high, medium, low, and none
levels. Persist priorities while keeping existing saved data compatible
and preserving task order and search behavior.

Document the command and test parsing, display, persistence, rollback,
and end-to-end CLI behavior.
